positions.as_written: Ask whether there was a single moment, since its absence points to an overuse presentation.
Take a jump volume history in a player with anterior knee pain.
Expect apophyseal problems rather than tendinopathy in a skeletally immature player.
Use jump count as the manageable dose, since it is countable where other exposures are not.
Expect imaging change and symptoms to correlate imperfectly in tendinopathy.
State that jump count is a proxy and that tendon stress is not measured.

Weigh the player's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations, because load restriction in a selected squad player is a harder conversation than it looks.
